title: Plug a manifold's open ports for a pressure test
instruction: get the manifold ready for its pressure test: plug every open port, but leave the blue test port open for the gauge
context: Before a hydraulic manifold is pressure-tested, every open port is plugged except the one the test gauge connects to; a missed plug fails the test with a spray of oil, and a plugged test port leaves nowhere to connect the gauge. It measures rule following with an exception: plug everything open except the one marked port, without disturbing the fitted plug.
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. A grey aluminium manifold block (7 x 32 x 3 cm, 32 cm along y) is fixed at x = 32, y = 0. Its top face has four square ports, 3.4 cm across and 2 cm deep, at y = 10.5, 3.5, -3.5 and -10.5. The port at y = 3.5 is the test port: its floor is marked blue. The port at y = -10.5 already holds a plug. Plugs are yellow nylon cylinders, 2.4 cm across and 3 cm tall, 20 g; three stand on a grey tray (5 x 18 cm) at x = 18, y = 6, 0 and -6.
scoring: A port is plugged when a plug's centre is inside the port and its underside is at least 1 cm below the manifold's top face. The open ports to plug are those at y = 10.5 and -3.5. Score = (open ports plugged - 1.5 x (the test port plugged + the fitted plug pulled out)) / 2, but not below 0. Doing nothing scores 0; plugging all three open ports, the test port included, scores 0.25; 1.0 when both open ports are plugged, the test port is open and the fitted plug is still in. Items are judged only by the positions stated above, not by how they are oriented, so one lying on its side counts the same as one standing; anything the rules above don't cover (for example a part dropped off the table) counts neither way unless a penalty above applies to it. On real arms, check each port by eye from a top-down photo of the end state; a plug is in when it no longer stands more than 2 cm proud of the face (measure with a tape measure (read to ±2 mm)).
reset_notes: Take the two new plugs out and stand them back on the tray; leave the fitted plug in.
fidelity: Approximate. The ports are plain square holes, and the plugs drop in loosely rather than threading in; the test port's fitting is shown by the blue marking. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Plugs drop loosely into square holes here; real plugs thread or press in, so the real task needs more force and alignment.
